title: Model Admission Metadata Shim & Route-level Fallback Contract
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket clarifies a lightweight admission contract for new open-model entries that cannot be immediately hard-pinned to a specific runtime. Instead of blocking these models or forcing full pinning, we propose a metadata 'shim' approach: each catalog entry provides a minimal, machine-readable compatibility metadata payload plus a per-route fallback contract. The runtime and Console use that metadata to enable automated soft normalization and deterministic fallback behavior when minor incompatibilities are detected (tokenizer differences, kv cache key shapes, preferred quantization profile, or required attention kernel hints).

Background / Problem:
- Many community/open models arrive with subtle runtime incompatibilities that are low risk but prevent safe unpinned serving (tokenizer EOS behavior, different padding semantics, kv-cache layout assumptions).
- Current options are either: (1) fully pin the variant to a tested runtime (reduces agility) or (2) allow unpinned variants which sometimes cause customer-facing errors or silent quality regressions.
- PM needs a clarified acceptance surface so that product, runtime, and DX teams can accept more models into the catalog safely while preserving rollout flexibility.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Compatibility Metadata Shim: require a small JSON metadata block at intake with a bounded set of fields (see "Required metadata fields" below). This metadata is stored with the catalog entry and surfaced in the Console. It is machine-readable and runtime-consumable.
2) Route-level Fallback Contract: catalog entries must include a fallback mapping indicating compatible variants or canonical transforms the runtime can apply when a mismatch occurs (e.g., remap tokenizer IDs, normalize trailing spaces, enable "legacy-token-padding" flag).
3) Automated Pre-checks: Intake pipeline runs a suite of fast sanity checks derived from the shim (tokenizer roundtrips for 20 prompts, KV cache token shape probe, quantization compatibility probe). Results are recorded and require at least a 95% pass rate for acceptance to the "experimental" ring.
4) Console UX + Warnings: the Console shows explicit compatibility score, required normalization flags, and recommended pin level (unpinned, soft-pin, hard-pin). Users can opt into auto-normalization on a per-route basis.

Required metadata fields (minimal intake contract):
- tokenizer_schema: string (e.g., "bpe-v1-with-eos-consume" or "sentencepiece-v2")
- kv_layout: string (e.g., "kv-v1-interleaved" or "kv-v2-separate")
- preferred_quant: string (e.g., "int8-q4_k_m", "fp16")
- fallbacks: list of variant aliases or runtime flags (comma-separated string allowed)
- compat_severity_hint: one of ["minor", "moderate", "major"]
- suggested_pin: one of ["unpinned", "soft-pin", "hard-pin"]

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Building full tokenizer adapters that rewrite tokenizers end-to-end (we only allow deterministic remapping/transforms documented in the shim).
- Long-running re-compilations for every new variant (those belong to runtime optimization backlog).

Acceptance criteria (see separate list field)

Implementation notes / Tradeoffs:
- Benefits: allows more community models to be visible and usable quickly, gives runtime deterministic fallback behavior, makes Console guidance actionable for customers.
- Risks: inaccurate shim values could give false confidence; to mitigate we require runtime probes and a manual review flag for "moderate/major" severity.
- Tradeoff: we accept some additional complexity in the intake pipeline in exchange for reducing hard-pin load on runtime teams.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (catalog-only, internal): implement metadata schema + intake validation + Console display behind feature flag (2 sprints).
- Phase 2 (experimental ring): enable auto-normalization for routes in experimental ring where shim probes pass (1 sprint).
- Phase 3 (public): open to wider catalog intake and document operational runbooks (1 sprint + docs).
acceptance_criteria: Metadata schema implemented in intake service and validated against sample entries (unit tests added)
Intake pipeline runs 3 fast probes (tokenizer roundtrip, kv-layout probe, quantization probe) and stores results in the catalog record
Console surfaces compat_severity_hint, suggested_pin, and a click-to-run probe action for reviewers
Runtime exposes a deterministic 'normalization' flag and implements at least 2 normalization transforms (trailing-EOS normalization, tokenizer-id remap) documented in the shim
Auto-normalization can be toggled per-route via Console and routes with auto-normalization enabled have successful E2E smoke tests (>=95% pass on 20 sample prompts)
Onboarded 3 internal test models using the shim workflow and documented the manual review checklist
Monitoring: add a fallback counter metric and a quality-regression alert (regression if rollback-rate > 2% within 24h)
PRs: intake validation PR and Console changes merged and linked in ticket
Documentation: intake spec and runbook published in Confluence (link below)

2026-03-05 - Design: Console wording suggestions: replace 'compat_severity_hint' with 'compatibility risk' and show color banding; prefer toggles for auto-normalization per route.
2026-03-09 - Compliance: no additional KMS or secret handling required for shim metadata. Marked security_review_required=false.

notes: Decision: require at least tokenizer_schema and fallbacks to accept a model into the experimental ring
If a model reports compat_severity_hint=major it must be hard-pinned and undergo full runtime validation before public catalog listing
